title: Faster file previews
summary: Large PDFs now *stream* instead of waiting for the full download, so the first page shows in under a second.
author: JeVaughn + Claude

steps.title: Open big PDFs without the wait
steps.narration: A 90MB contract took *8 seconds* to preview because we downloaded the whole file first. Goal: show page one immediately.
bullets: Find where previews fetch the file
Swap full download for range requests
Keep a fallback for servers without range support
steps.voiceover: So the problem. A ninety megabyte contract took about eight seconds to preview, because we downloaded the entire file before showing anything. The goal was to show page one right away.

steps.title: Traced the slow path
steps.narration: Every preview type funnels through one helper that calls *fetchAll*. PDFs were the only type that didn't need it.
steps.voiceover: I traced the slow path first. Every preview type goes through one helper that downloads the whole file, and PDFs were the one type that didn't actually need that.

steps.title: Stream the first page
steps.narration: Replaced the full download with a *ranged read* of the first chunk, then hand that straight to the renderer.

lines.s: const pdf = await loadPdf(stream, { lazy: true })

steps.voiceover: The fix itself is small. Instead of the full download, we read just the first chunk of the file with a range request, and hand it straight to the renderer.

steps.title: Range requests over thumbnails
steps.narration: Pre-rendering would be faster still, but needs a *background worker* we don't have yet.

options.label: HTTP range requests
options.why: Works with the S3 setup we already have

steps.voiceover: We did consider pre-rendering thumbnails on upload. It would be even faster, but it needs a background worker we don't have yet, so range requests won.

steps.title: Tests green, 90MB file in 0.7s
steps.narration: Added cases for the *416 fallback* and checked a real 90MB contract by hand.
steps.voiceover: Tests are green. All forty-eight pass, including new ones for servers that don't support range requests. And that ninety megabyte file now opens in about point seven seconds.

steps.title: PR up for review
steps.narration: Opened the PR with before/after timings. Preview env is deployed for anyone who wants to try it.
steps.voiceover: The pull request is up with before and after timings, and it's deployed to the preview environment if anyone wants to try it.

next: Progress bar while later pages load

voiceover.intro: Here's today's update. The big one: large PDFs used to make you wait for the whole download. Now they stream, so the first page shows up in under a second.
voiceover.outro: Next up, I want to give video previews the same treatment, and add a progress bar while the later pages load. That's the update.
